newsitem.title: GREECE: EU SAYS GREECE MUST SPEED UP FUND ABSORPTION.
newsitem.headline: EU SAYS GREECE MUST SPEED UP FUND ABSORPTION.

text.p: European Commissioner for Employment and Social Affairs Padraeg Flynn told Greece on Monday that it had a low fund absorption rate and must hurry to meet a 1999 deadline.

"However, the Prime Minister has assured me that there will be a significant upgrading and speeding up of human resource training and development programmes in the remaining two years," he told reporters in Athens.
Flynn said he came to Greece to express his concern about the low fund absorption rate with regard to the development of human resources.
Greece has an absorption rate of 23.5 percent. Out of 2.5 billion Ecu allocated in 1993 for health, labour and educational programmes, only a fourth has been absorbed, he said.
Although he said he received unfulfilled promises from Greece in the past, he was confident that this time the Greek government appeared determined to do its best to implement such programmes.
Flynn also discussed specific plans presented to him by the Ministers of Education, Health and Labour on new and better programmes, and warned Greece to act before it was too late.
"Emphasis must be placed on training and skills development as the labour market is becoming global and Greeks should be prepared", he said.

He admitted that there are weaknesses in the management of funds that cause delays and issued a warning, saying that Greece should act now before it is too late. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
